newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bond curve flattens as money rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bond curve flattens as money rates rise.

text.p: The yield curve of Belgian linear bonds flattened sharply on Thursday as money market rates continued to rise and long bond prices moved higher on the back of a firmer overnight United States market, traders said.
"There is really good flattening going on. The short end of the curve is very much under pressure," one trader said.
"The Belgian central bank is squeezing liquidity to support the franc and rates and therefore the short end are going up, up, up," another trader said.
However, traders noted that the actual volume of business was relatively low and confined to domestic players.
The one week repo rate was 3.75/80 at 1000 GMT compared with 3.71/78 at 0745 GMT and 3.67/72 late on Wednesday.
The mark/franc rate was 20.6485/00 against 20.6464/74 late on Wednesday.
The benchmark 10-year OLO was yielding 5.63 percent against 5.68 late on Wednesday, but the spread over German Bunds was static at eight basis points.
The front month futures contract was 35 basis points higher at 122.23.
